newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle off $1 at $65,light-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle off $1 at $65,light-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle prices Wednesday turned $1.00 per cwt lower in light trading late at $65.00, according to USDA and feedlot sources said.
An estimated 4,700 steers and heifers that will likely grade choice and select sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, USDA said.
There were 42,700 head in the Panhandle confirmed for the week to date, including 31,400 formulated cattle to be shipped this week, according to USDA.
The bulk of cattle, however, remain priced at $67.00 as owners hold out for $66.00, feedlot sources said.
Weakness was attributed to lower beef prices at midday and a slide in Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures, the sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.85 to $1.31 per cwt, with 275 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.

Kansas feedlots reported only light sales of heifers at $66.50 early that were shipped to Nebraska from northwest Kansas, according to USDA. The heifers were expected to grade select to mostly choice. Several feedlot managers said owners still anticipated steady prices ($66.00) this week on light supplies of finished cattle.
